Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the redacted certificate. I looped in Priyom from Tax Ops to confirm acceptance criteria, but below is what typically clears a subscription invoice hold with us: 

- A signed state resale certificate (PDF) that includes the buyer name and EIN and explicitly lists the type of transaction ("purchase for resale" or equivalent). Redactions that remove the EIN usually fail acceptance.
- If the certificate format omits a clear seller/buyer mapping, a short signed attestation on company letterhead stating: the transaction is for resale, the Redwood invoices will be resold to end customers, an effective date, and an authorized signature.
- For multi-invoice releases, include a simple mapping: invoice number -> PO / ship-to / end-customer name (if applicable).

I'll attach our acceptance checklist to make it easy for AP. If you can send a signed attestation plus either an unredacted certificate or a notarized copy, we should be able to release at least two of the three invoices the same day. INV-8153 might need the EIN filled in.

If you prefer, I can provisionally release invoices with a signed attestation plus a follow-up that supplies the full certificate within 7 business days — let me know which route you prefer.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_exemption_acceptance_checklist.pdf (pdf, 58 KB)]

Hi all — quick tax ops guidance from my side: 

1) Evidence: we need either (A) a state-issued resale certificate listing Atlas Town & Co as purchaser and showing effective date and EIN, or (B) a company-signed attestation on letterhead that contains: purchaser legal name, EIN, a statement that the purchase is for resale, the nature of goods/services ("cloud software/subscription for resale"), effective date, and authorized signature.

2) Jurisdictions: which states are you claiming exemption in? SaaS rules vary; if Island State (example) requires a specific statutory citation, include that.

3) Mapping: include invoice number -> PO -> Redwood bill-to name (Redwood Inference, Inc., EIN: XX-XXXXXXX). If invoices are for different Atlas legal entities, we must receive a certificate for each entity.

4) Timing: if the attestation is signed and includes the EIN, we can release invoices within 24 hours. If the attestation is provided but the certificate is outstanding, we can set temporary release (holds converted to conditional release) for up to 7 business days pending receipt of the full certificate.

Sample attestation wording (feel free to paste into your letterhead):
"On behalf of Atlas Town & Co (EIN: 12-3456789), I certify that purchases of cloud software subscriptions from Redwood Inference are intended for resale to our end customers and are therefore exempt under state resale statutes effective 2024-01-01. Signed: [authorized signatory]"

Attaching a short sample file for AP to use.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Tax Operations | Redwood Inference
